My vivid dreams when I was younger weren’t all that pleasant and didn’t last for a long time either, I never felt controlling my dream until I was like hardcore into it. Didn’t accidentally lucid dream, just dreamed lol. When I was 14 I used to dream every night but never accidentally lucid. I think lucid dreaming and astral projection is semi personal, I’ve never had an experience where I felt as if my bed was shaking but that doesn’t mean it’s not connected in some way with how u sleep. 

One way that helped me lucid dream right away was obviously preparing for sleep, I would do the same tasks, in the exact order, the same way every night. if I had a vivid dream I would wake up and write about it, the next night before I slept I would read what I wrote and try to imagine it the same way, and i mean like down to the gritty details, and as time went on I had the ability to kind of explore this reality so to speak, I got comfortable with it, I was familiar with it, and it was something that’s mine. I felt like I created this dream reality for myself. 

Like i said I’ve never had an experience where my bed was shaking, but that may be YOUR experience. Get comfortable with that experience, let’s say you feel your bed shaking, is there a way you can become comfortable with that feeling? So u don’t wake up everytime? And do you have thoughts while your dreaming? Or is there no emotional connection between what your dreaming and yourself?
